What you read is a **view** of the song, not the song: a header, one block per bar, then the automation lanes. It carries every id and every field the tools take. Below it are six descriptive axes — rhythm, harmony, melody, texture, form and within-song variation.

Rules that are not negotiable, because the tools enforce them anyway:

- Use the ids the view gives you, and the ids a tool's result returns. Do not invent an id, and do not write `id`, `version` or `provenance` — those are the editor's.
- A call that is refused comes back with every rule it broke. Read them all and call again.

Two things about what you are doing:

- **Nothing you do is applied.** Your calls build a proposal, and a person reads the whole change as one diff and applies, rejects or edits it. Say what you changed in the proposal, never that you changed the song.
- The axes are **counts over this document**, not judgements. No key, genre or norm is claimed; a sampler voice's pitches may not be pitches. Use them to check what you meant against what you did. A person decides.

Answer in plain prose when you are done calling tools.

function.name: apply_patch
function.description:
Apply an RFC 6902 patch directly. The typed tools below are the supported surface; this exists because M0.4 must drive core through the tool API rather than the file (CLAUDE.md #2), and because §9 lets a user edit a proposed diff before applying it.

An op writing an entity's `version` is refused: core maintains it (ADR 0005 §3).

patch.description: Canonical RFC 6902 text, the same form ToolResult.patch returns.

function.name: add_track
function.description:
Adds a track. `index` is assigned after the current last; the master track already exists in every song (§4.4).

`ref` is required when `kind` is TRACK_KIND_INSTRUMENT and refused otherwise: ADR 0002 requires an instrument present exactly when the track is one, so an instrument track cannot be created empty and filled in afterwards — there is no valid song in between.

function.name: set_track_instrument
function.description: Sets the instrument on an instrument track. Replaces whatever was there.

ref.description: The device is identified by which case is set; there is no separate kind (ADR 0002 §3).

function.name: add_effect
function.description: Adds an effect to a track's chain.

index.description: Position in the chain. Absent appends after the current last.

function.name: add_clip
function.description: Adds a clip to a track.

fade_in_ticks.description: Ramps at the clip's edges, clip-relative, in ticks — the model's one time base (§4.2). 0 is no fade. Linear in amplitude, and the two ramps multiply, so fades that overlap need no rule (ADR 0011 §2).

gain_db.description: Clip gain. 0.0 is unity. An audio track has no device, so no ParamRef can reach this; without it a hot clip has no fix short of editing the asset (ADR 0011 §1).

time_stretch.description: Stretch the asset, pitch unchanged, to fill the clip's musical length: loop_length_ticks if it loops, length_ticks otherwise. A flag rather than a ratio, because the ratio derives from the asset's duration and core reads no file (ADR 0011 §3).

expression.description: Per-note expression (§4.2). Key: parameter name, e.g. "timbre".

function.name: set_notes
function.description: Replaces the clip's whole note set. A note carrying an id that already exists in this clip keeps it; every other note is minted a new one.

expression.description: Per-note expression (§4.2). Key: parameter name, e.g. "timbre".

function.name: transpose
function.description: Adds `semitones` to each note's pitch. A result outside MIDI 0-127 is refused, never clamped: silently rewriting a caller's request is how a tool stops being predictable.

note_ids.description: Empty means every note in the clip.

function.name: quantize
function.description: Snaps each note's start_tick to the nearest multiple of grid_ticks. Integer arithmetic throughout, with a fixed tie rule, so the result cannot vary by platform (§11).

function.name: add_automation
function.description: Adds an automation lane for one device parameter, with its points.

function.name: set_tempo
function.description: Upserts the tempo event at `tick`. The map must keep an event at tick 0 (§4.4).

function.name: add_section
function.description: Adds a named section over a range of ticks. Sections label time; they contain nothing.

function.name: move_section
function.description: Moves a section's bounds. Its clips do not move: §4.2 makes a section a label over a time range, not a container.

function.name: apply_patch
function.description:
Apply an RFC 6902 patch directly. The typed tools below are the supported surface; this exists because M0.4 must drive core through the tool API rather than the file (CLAUDE.md #2), and because §9 lets a user edit a proposed diff before applying it.

An op writing an entity's `version` is refused: core maintains it (ADR 0005 §3).

patch.description: Canonical RFC 6902 text, the same form ToolResult.patch returns.

function.name: add_track
function.description:
Adds a track. `index` is assigned after the current last; the master track already exists in every song (§4.4).

`ref` is required when `kind` is TRACK_KIND_INSTRUMENT and refused otherwise: ADR 0002 requires an instrument present exactly when the track is one, so an instrument track cannot be created empty and filled in afterwards — there is no valid song in between.

function.name: set_track_instrument
function.description: Sets the instrument on an instrument track. Replaces whatever was there.

ref.description: The device is identified by which case is set; there is no separate kind (ADR 0002 §3).

function.name: add_effect
function.description: Adds an effect to a track's chain.

index.description: Position in the chain. Absent appends after the current last.

function.name: add_clip
function.description: Adds a clip to a track.

fade_in_ticks.description: Ramps at the clip's edges, clip-relative, in ticks — the model's one time base (§4.2). 0 is no fade. Linear in amplitude, and the two ramps multiply, so fades that overlap need no rule (ADR 0011 §2).

gain_db.description: Clip gain. 0.0 is unity. An audio track has no device, so no ParamRef can reach this; without it a hot clip has no fix short of editing the asset (ADR 0011 §1).

time_stretch.description: Stretch the asset, pitch unchanged, to fill the clip's musical length: loop_length_ticks if it loops, length_ticks otherwise. A flag rather than a ratio, because the ratio derives from the asset's duration and core reads no file (ADR 0011 §3).

expression.description: Per-note expression (§4.2). Key: parameter name, e.g. "timbre".

function.name: set_notes
function.description: Replaces the clip's whole note set. A note carrying an id that already exists in this clip keeps it; every other note is minted a new one.

expression.description: Per-note expression (§4.2). Key: parameter name, e.g. "timbre".

function.name: transpose
function.description: Adds `semitones` to each note's pitch. A result outside MIDI 0-127 is refused, never clamped: silently rewriting a caller's request is how a tool stops being predictable.

note_ids.description: Empty means every note in the clip.

function.name: quantize
function.description: Snaps each note's start_tick to the nearest multiple of grid_ticks. Integer arithmetic throughout, with a fixed tie rule, so the result cannot vary by platform (§11).

function.name: add_automation
function.description: Adds an automation lane for one device parameter, with its points.

function.name: set_tempo
function.description: Upserts the tempo event at `tick`. The map must keep an event at tick 0 (§4.4).

function.name: add_section
function.description: Adds a named section over a range of ticks. Sections label time; they contain nothing.

function.name: move_section
function.description: Moves a section's bounds. Its clips do not move: §4.2 makes a section a label over a time range, not a container.

message.content:
The proposal adds a **Lead** track and one 4-bar-length clip of four notes over the bass.

- **Track**: `Lead` (id `…0034`), instrument track with a Surge XT plugin device (`…0035`), same as the Bass.
- **Clip**: `…0036` on Lead, start tick 0, length 3840, four notes, one per beat:
  - C4 (60) at 0, E4 (64) at 960, G4 (67) at 1920, C5 (72) at 2880 — each 960 ticks long, velocities 96/92/98/104.

What the axes now read: the song goes from 1 onset to 5, all still on beats, syncopation 0, smallest gap 960. Harmony gains E and G alongside the bass's C (C 2880, E 960, G 960 ticks of mass, chromaticism 0). The Lead line is range 60–72, 4 distinct pitches, intervals +4 +3 +5, all ascending, no steps. Texture is 2 voices, mean simultaneity 1, Lead sounding the full 3840. Form is still one distinct bar; both voices now enter at bar 1.

Two things worth your eye before applying: the lead sits entirely in the upper register with no rests, so it's a continuous quarter-note line rather than a phrase with breathing room; and the pitches are a plain C-major arpeggio, which is a choice I made, not one the bass forced — the bass only gives C.
